title: The no-context fallback, and the boundary that keeps it from swallowing real abstention
goal: Prove lab.common.open_domain's no-context fallback (FORBIDDEN.md, 2026-10-16) answers correctly and visibly-disclaimed when passages is genuinely empty, and -- the more important check -- that a real retrieval miss (passages given, none relevant) is completely unaffected and still abstains the original way.
method: 3 genuinely-no-context asks through brain.reason(ask, []), checked for decision=='ungrounded', the fixed disclaimer prefix, and no fabricated citation marker. 1 retrieval-miss case (passages given, ask about something not in them) checked against the unchanged pre-existing abstain behavior. 1 genuine evidence-grounded case as a regression check on the existing path.

cases.ask: What is the capital of France?
cases.text: [Not grounded in any provided evidence -- general knowledge only.] The capital of France is Paris.

cases.ask: What is the boiling point of water in Celsius?
cases.text: [Not grounded in any provided evidence -- general knowledge only.] The boiling point of water is 100°C.

cases.ask: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
cases.text: [Not grounded in any provided evidence -- general knowledge only.] The play Romeo and Juliet was written by William Shakespeare.

results_prose: No-context fallback: 3/3 asks correctly answered with decision='ungrounded', the fixed disclaimer, and no fabricated citation marker. The boundary check: a real retrieval miss (passages given, none relevant) still correctly abstains (decision='inconclusive'). The existing evidence-grounded path is unaffected (decision='supported', text='30 days [B1]').
conclusion: The no-context fallback works and, critically, stays exactly where FORBIDDEN.md's exception draws the line: a genuinely empty passages list gets an explicitly disclaimed, ungrounded answer, while a real retrieval miss -- passages were given, just none of them relevant -- still abstains exactly as it did before this branch existed. The two cases are structurally distinguished (checked before any retrieval runs, not by a confidence score), so there is no way for a struggling retrieval to slide into the ungrounded path and dodge abstention.
scale_down: 3 no-context asks, 1 retrieval-miss case, 1 genuine case -- enough to prove the mechanism and its boundary, not a broad open-domain QA benchmark.
follow_ups: Only gemma3:270m via Ollama tested for this role; flan-t5-small (also permitted by the exception) not yet measured here.

The citation-marker rejection has only been exercised when the model happens not to fabricate one; a case that reliably provokes a fabricated marker (to prove the rejection actually fires) has not been constructed.
models_used: gemma3:270m via Ollama, in the new no-context role (FORBIDDEN.md 2026-10-16) -- not the rewriter role, a third, separate, narrowly-scoped generative use.
